status: proposal: starting values, tune against real shoot nights and record changes in docs/ios/PLAN.md §Verdict

aerosol_optical_depth.label: Haze / smoke (AOD, 550 nm)
aerosol_optical_depth.note: Total column (CAMS, 550 nm). At GC culmination in Utah (airmass 2.6-2.9) 0.10 costs ~0.4 stop and 0.25 ~1 stop of Milky Way signal; clean Utah background is 0.02-0.07 (AERONET NEON_MOAB/NEON_ONAQ 2016-2025). Researched 2026-09-26.

smoke_column.label: Smoke overhead (RAP-Smoke, vertically integrated)
smoke_column.note: Worst hour in window. Smoke AOD = 0.0045 x column (mg/m2); with a 0.05 background, 10 and 40 match the AOD edges 0.10 and 0.25 (docs/methods.md). Models tend to underpredict smoke AOD (Ye et al. 2021): do not loosen without logged nights.

pm2_5.label: Surface smoke (PM2.5)
pm2_5.note: Advisory: surface health signal, not sky transparency. Edges are the EPA 2024 AQI Good/Moderate breakpoints. Utah 2016-2025: surface PM2.5 missed 79-94% of fire-season AOD>0.25 days and reads high under winter inversions with AOD ~0.04.

aqi_pm25_observed.label: Observed AQI, PM2.5 only (AirNow NowCast)
aqi_pm25_observed.note: Advisory, never a go signal; ignore ozone rows. Jun-Oct, AQI>100 coincided with AOD>0.25 on 83-100% of days (Wasatch Front monitors vs AERONET NEON_ONAQ, 2016-2025). Candidate no-go confirmer once the verdict engine supports a PM2.5-only, Jun-Oct or smoke-present rule where no nearby monitor means no signal, not incomplete data.

dust.label: Surface dust (CAMS)
dust.note: Shown only. Column dust is already in the AOD factor; no evidence found for a surface-dust threshold.

seeing.label: Seeing (7Timer scale 1–8, 1 best)
seeing.note: Wide-field Milky Way work barely notices seeing. Shown for long-lens nights.

dew_point_spread.label: Temperature minus dew point
dew_point_spread.note: Advisory: below the marginal value, say 'bring a dew heater', not 'don't go'.

gc_max_altitude.label: Galactic Center peak altitude in window
gc_max_altitude.note: Gates only when the plan's target is the Milky Way core. Marginal matches app-config gc_min_useful_altitude_deg.

kp_index.label: Aurora chance (planetary Kp)
kp_index.note: Never lowers the verdict. At or above the latitude-dependent visible Kp, the verdict gets an 'aurora possible' flag.
kp_index.latitude_basis_note: SWPC: the Kp-to-oval relationship 'holds true in geomagnetic latitude, not geographic' (spaceweather.gov/content/tips-viewing-aurora). Centered-dipole latitude from the pole below: Salt Lake City 47.6, Moab 45.7, St George 43.8, Glacier NP 55.2, about 7 degrees above their geographic latitudes.

geomagnetic_north_pole.source: NOAA NCEI, Wandering of the Geomagnetic Poles: WMM2025 geomagnetic north pole for 2025.0, 80.85 N (geodetic) 72.76 W (https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/wandering-geomagnetic-poles). The dipole axis moves a few hundredths of a degree a year; refresh with WMM2030.

kp_index.visible_kp_source: NOAA Space Weather Scales (spaceweather.gov/noaa-scales-explanation), aurora line per G level: G2 Kp 6 'typically 55 geomagnetic lat', G3 Kp 7 '50', G4 'Kp = 8, including a 9-' '45', G5 Kp 9 '40'; G1 gives no latitude, so it has no row. kp_min is the level's lowest third: SWPC labels a Kp of 4.67 (5-) as G1, and a G level spans N-, No, N+ (Sharpe and Murray 2017, Space Weather; arXiv:1804.02985), except that NOAA puts 9- in G4, so G5 starts at 9.0. Checked 2026-09-26.
kp_index.visible_kp_note: A spot's visible Kp is the lowest kp_min whose geomagnetic_lat_min_deg is at or below the spot's absolute geomagnetic latitude; below the last row, no flag. Kp rows are 3-hour intervals starting at their time tag. The flag is raised by the latest observed Kp (its interval contains now or ended within one interval) for the next dark window, or by any observed or forecast interval overlapping the night's astronomical darkness. OVATION '% near this cell' is not used: it is an overhead probability for the 3x3 degree box around the cell with a 30-90 min lead, while SWPC notes aurora 'can be observed from as much as 1000 km away' (spaceweather.gov/products/aurora-30-minute-forecast). The G-scale latitudes describe where aurora 'has been seen'; a camera records fainter aurora, so tune against logged nights instead of loosening here.
